name: Furniture, fixtures & equipment (FF&E) and operating supplies & equipment (OS&E)
notes: FF&E is OUTSIDE the baseline hard cost (see README hardCost definition). Hotel FF&E per HVS includes guestroom/public furniture, softgoods, kitchen & laundry equipment and technology; Marriott FDD Item 7 splits 'Furniture and Fixtures', 'Kitchen and Laundry Equipment', 'Technology' and 'Operating Supplies' (OS&E). Commercial kitchen equipment for restaurants lives in specialty-mep (commercial-kitchen), not here.

items.name: Hotel FF&E — limited-service / midscale extended-stay (per key)

cost.method: HVS 2026 survey (2025 budgets) limited-service FF&E median $16,079 / avg $18,020 (e7); HVS 2025 survey (2024 budgets) median $16,991 / avg $16,233 (e3). StudioRes FDD 2025: furniture & fixtures $12,200–15,900 + kitchen/laundry $2,100–2,700 = $14,300–18,600 per key (e12, e13). Mid $16,500 ≈ mean of the two HVS medians; low $13,500 ≈ StudioRes low less ~5%; high $19,500 ≈ above HVS 2026 average. Mixed 2024/2025 evidence (≤1 yr) expressed in 2025 $.

items.notes: Hampton/Fairfield/Tru/WoodSpring class. Includes kitchen/laundry equipment and in-room tech per HVS definition.

items.name: Hotel FF&E — select-service / upscale extended-stay (per key)

cost.method: HVS select-service FF&E: 2026 survey median $18,321 / avg $22,860 (e5, 2025 $); 2025 survey median $22,929 / avg $23,120 (e1, 2024 $). Marriott FDDs for prototype select brands: Fairfield furniture & fixtures $12,200–16,800 + kitchen/laundry $1,400–2,400 (e9, e10; 2023 $, older than 1 yr — used for the low end only), StudioRes $12,200–15,900 + $2,100–2,700 (e12, e13). Mid $21,000 = mean of the four HVS median/average values for 2025 and 2024 surveys ($21,808) rounded down for the newer, lower 2026 median; low $15,000 ≈ FDD furniture+kitchen low end; high $27,000 ≈ 2025 HVS average + ~15% for upscale ES/dual-brand public space.

items.notes: Courtyard/Hilton Garden Inn/Hyatt Place/AC/Residence Inn class. Excludes OS&E (see ose-hotel) and pre-opening.

items.name: Hotel FF&E — full-service (per key)

cost.method: HVS full-service FF&E: 2026 survey median $36,752 / avg $43,928 (e6, 2025 $); 2025 survey median $34,464 / avg $39,907 (e2, 2024 $). Westin FDD 2025 (250 keys): furniture & fixtures $34,800–44,500 + kitchen/laundry $7,800–10,000 + technology $2,800–9,200 = $45,400–63,700 per key (e15–e17). Mid $42,000 ≈ midpoint between HVS 2026 median and average ($40,340) nudged toward the FDD prototype; low $32,000 ≈ below HVS 2025 median; high $60,000 ≈ Westin FDD upper total.

items.notes: Marriott/Westin/Hilton/Hyatt Regency class incl. meeting space and F&B outlets furniture, kitchen and laundry equipment.

cost.method: HVS luxury FF&E: 2026 survey median $138,317 / avg $118,359 (e8, 2025 $); 2025 survey median $94,613 / avg $96,752 (e4, 2024 $). Mid $120,000 ≈ mean of the four values ($112,010) rounded up toward the newer survey; low $90,000 ≈ 2025 survey median less ~5%; high $160,000 ≈ 2026 median + 15%. Small luxury samples — wide spread.

items.name: Hotel OS&E — limited/select-service opening operating supplies (per key)

cost.method: Marriott FDD 'Operating Supplies' (towels, linens, guestroom amenities, maintenance supplies, paper goods, uniforms): StudioRes 2025 $186,000–248,000 for 124 keys = $1,500–2,000/key (e14); Fairfield 2023 $150,100–208,800 for 80–110 keys = $1,365 (150,100/110) to $2,610 (208,800/80)/key (e11, 2023 $ — older than 1 yr, used for spread only). Mid $1,900 ≈ midpoint of StudioRes per-key range + small allowance for F&B smallwares; low/high = Fairfield per-key extremes rounded.

items.notes: Opening inventory only; separate from pre-opening labor/marketing (soft cost). For full-service use ose-hotel-full.

items.name: Hotel OS&E — full-service opening operating supplies incl. china/glass/silver (per key)

cost.method: Westin FDD 2025: Operating Supplies $6,600–8,500 per guestroom plus $48,000–61,400 per hotel (250 keys → +$190–250/key) (e18). Low = $6,600; high = $8,500 + $250 ≈ $8,800; mid $7,600 ≈ midpoint ($7,550 + ~$220 fixed share) rounded. Single brand source — verify with operator OS&E budget.

items.notes: Includes uniforms, china, flatware, towels, linens, amenities and banquet smallwares.

items.name: Multifamily common-area & amenity FF&E (clubhouse, leasing, fitness, lobby) — per unit

cost.method: Derived. Assumes 20–40 SF of furnished common/amenity area per unit (e.g., 5,000–8,000 SF clubhouse+leasing+fitness for 250 units) × office-grade furniture at Cushman & Wakefield 2026 furniture benchmarks $23–61/SF (e19–e21) ≈ $460–2,440/unit, plus fitness equipment (~$60–80k per 250 units ≈ $250–320/unit). Low $750 ≈ 20 SF × $25 + $250; mid $1,500 ≈ 28 SF × $42 + $300; high $3,000 ≈ 40 SF × $61 + coworking/amenity-rich luxury allowance. Units themselves are unfurnished.

items.notes: Excludes in-unit appliances (in hard cost) and furnished-unit packages.

items.name: Student housing FF&E — furnished bedroom + share of unit living room (per bed)

cost.method: Derived from hotel prototype furniture packages: Marriott economy/select 'Furniture and Fixtures' $12,200–16,800 per guestroom (e9, e12) covers casegoods, seating, softgoods, lighting, a TV and a share of public space. A student bed package (XL twin bed + mattress, desk, chair, dresser/wardrobe, share of living-room sofa/table) ≈ 25–40% of a hotel key: 0.25 × $12,200 ≈ $3,050 (low) to 0.40 × $16,300 ≈ $6,500 (high); mid $4,500 ≈ 0.32 × $14,000. Includes share of lounge/study furniture. Verify with student-housing FF&E vendor pricing.

items.notes: Purpose-built off-campus student housing furnished by the owner.

items.name: Senior living FF&E — common areas, dining, activity, memory-care furnishings (per unit)

cost.method: Derived. Residents furnish their own IL/AL apartments, so FF&E is mostly public space (dining, lounges, activity, therapy, salon), back-of-house kitchen/laundry smallwares and furnished memory-care rooms — closest analogue is select-service hotel public-space-heavy FF&E. HVS select-service FF&E $18,321–23,120/key (e1, e5) less the guestroom furniture share (~45–60%, per Fairfield FDD guestroom-focused F&F $12,200–16,800 vs kitchen/laundry $1,400–2,400, e10) ≈ $7,000–12,000; mid $11,000 adds commercial dining furniture density; high $16,000 for memory-care-heavy or luxury CCRC. Commercial kitchen equipment is separate (specialty-mep).

items.name: Office furniture (workstations, seating, conference) — per SF

cost.method: Cushman & Wakefield Office Fit Out Cost Guide 2026 supplement furniture ranges: Tier 3 markets $23.39–35.09/SF (24% of hard cost), Tier 2 $27.54–41.32 (20%), Tier 1 $38.83–60.67 (22%) (e19–e21). Low $23 = Tier 3 low; mid $35 = midpoint of Tier 2 ($34.43) rounded; high $61 = Tier 1 high. Note C&W tiers are market tiers, not quality tiers.

items.notes: Excludes IT/AV (C&W: IT ≈ 4%, A/V ≈ 12% of hard cost) and move costs.

items.name: Restaurant front-of-house FF&E (tables, chairs, booths, décor, POS) — per seat

cost.method: Derived — no fetchable franchise Item 7 or seat-level source this session. Built up per seat: commercial chair $150–400, ¼ of a 4-top table + base $75–200, booth/banquette share $0–400, décor/lighting/POS/smallwares share $150–500 → $400 (QSR loose seating) to $1,500 (full-service casual with booths); mid $800. Back-of-house kitchen equipment excluded (specialty-mep: commercial-kitchen). Verify with a franchise FDD Item 7 'furniture, fixtures & décor' line divided by seat count.

items.notes: Per dining seat. Bar equipment and walk-ins excluded.

items.name: Glamping unit furnishing (tent/dome/pod interior: bed, linens, seating, décor, heater/fan) — per unit

cost.method: Derived from hotel per-key packages. Economy/select prototype 'Furniture and Fixtures' $12,200–16,800 per key (e9, e12) includes carpet-free casegoods, softgoods, TV and public space; a glamping unit has a bed, nightstands, seating, rug, lighting, portable heat/cooling and outdoor furniture but no TV/public-space share: ≈ 40–60% of a hotel key ($5,000–9,800) + OS&E linens/amenities ≈ $1,500–2,000/key (e14). Mid $10,000 ≈ 0.6 × $14,000 + $1,600; high $18,000 = luxury safari tent with king bed, en-suite fixtures décor and deck furniture. Structure itself excluded.

items.notes: Per rentable glamping unit; structure, platform and utilities are separate items.

items.name: Short-term-rental cabin full furnishing incl. kitchenware & linens (per cabin key)

cost.method: Derived. Per bedroom ≈ 80% of a prototype hotel key furniture package ($12,200–16,800, e9/e12; less public-space share) and a living/dining/kitchenware package $3,000–6,000 incl. OS&E-type linens (cf. $1,500–2,000/key OS&E, e14). 1.5-BR equivalent: 1.5 × $12,200 × 0.8 + $3,000 ≈ $17,600 (low); 2.5-BR: 2.5 × $14,000 × 0.8 + $4,500 ≈ $32,500 → mid $30,000; 3-BR luxury: 3 × $16,800 × 0.8 + $6,000 ≈ $46,300 → high $50,000 incl. hot-tub accessories/game room. Verify with STR furnishing vendor quotes.

items.notes: One 'key' = one rentable cabin/home. Appliances assumed in the hard cost.
